To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

naturally arising CD25+ regulatory T cells play critical roles in the maintenance and control of peripheral immunologic self tolerance, and their deficiency or functional alteration leads to the development of autoimmune/inflammatory diseases.
naturally arising CD25+Foxp3+ regulatory T (nTreg) cells play key roles in maintaining immunologic self tolerance, and in the negative control of a broad spectrum of immune responses.

1) naturally arising Treg cells are a distinct subpopulation of T cells that express the Foxp3 transcription factor and play key roles in dominant control of self reactivity and prevention of autoimmune disease; 2) the Treg mediated dominant self tolerance is maintained by the Treg cell mediated suppression of self reactive T cells; and 3) Treg cells, which are highly dependent on IL 2 for their peripheral survival, are susceptible to IL 2 deficiency induced autoimmune diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular and cellular mechanism of Treg mediated dominant self tolerance and its breakdown in autoimmune disease, and the development of new methods for prevention and treatment of autoimmune disease.

the elucidation of the cellular and molecular basis of Treg mediated dominant self tolerance, and with the identification and functional characterization of novel molecules and signaling pathways that are involved in the development and function of natural Tregs and their control of self reactive T cells and autoimmune disease.

the Foxp3+CD4+CD25+ natural Tregs play a key role in maintaining immunologic self tolerance, and that their deficiency or dysfunction is associated with the development of autoimmune disease.

Foxp3+CD4+CD25+ T cells are the major natural Treg population in humans and mice, and that the Foxp3+ cells, which can be generated by TCR stimulation of CD4+CD25- naive T cells, are functionally indistinguishable from natural Tregs.

the Foxp3+CD4+CD25+ natural regulatory T (Tregs) play a critical role in the maintenance of dominant tolerance and negative control a variety of physiological/pathological immune responses.

the natural CD4+ Treg cell population is a major determinant of the peripheral balance between T cell tolerance and autoimmunity.
